Design problem: Design a car-mounted bicycle rack that addresses the following needs: (1) Easy mounting of the bicycle, (2) Easy mounting of the rack, (3) Cannot harm bike or car, and (4) Must be versatile for all bikes and cars.

Below is an example of a present day bike rack. The bicycle is set in the rails and the vinyl coated hook is attached to the seat tube of the bike, and then the hook is tightened down by hand with a wing nut. One should note the difficulty of mounting the middle bikes on the rack.

Please study the problem and this example. You will be asked to come up with your own designs later.

Quick question

What are you being asked to design in this study?

Idea generation

Early in a design process, designers use divergent thinking: coming up with many different possible solutions to a problem before choosing one to develop. The goal at this stage is to create multiple, diverse concepts.

In the parts that follow:

  • Generate varied, alternative concepts.
  • Sketch your concepts without worrying about your drawing skills. Rough sketches are fine.
  • Draw and describe each concept on its own concept sheet. Use Save and start a new concept to begin the next one. Sheets are numbered for you, and you can go back to edit any sheet using the Go to list above it.

Individual brainstorming

Brainstorming is a method for generating ideas. When brainstorming on your own:

  1. Postpone and withhold your judgment of ideas.
  2. Encourage wild and exaggerated ideas.
  3. Quantity counts at this stage, not quality.
  4. Build consecutively on your ideas.
  5. Every idea has equal worth.

Next, you will practice brainstorming on a practice problem for a few minutes.

description: This is a chair that allows the user to lean far back will sitting, with extra legs to support the slanted back.
This hollow cylinder shaped device allows the user to change orientation whenever.

This simple design is based on a bus bike rack. It attaches to the trunk of the car, then has a space to slot the bike in on its wheels, then it has an arm that swings over the front wheel to secure. The main pro of this method is that its easy to attach to the car, and easy to mount a bike on, but the cons are stability, and space usage.

This concept has an axle for the front fork, and two things keeping the back wheel in place, requiring you to remove the front wheel, place the bike on the roof of the car, attaching the front fork to the axle with nuts.
This design is just a tray that mounts on top of the car, with bungee cords on top that secure the bike to it (laid flat)

This mount goes on the back of the car and has a hook for the front wheel (with a little clasp), which it hangs from, and foam below to cushion the bike from bouncing against the car. There is also a cord which secures the bottom part of the bike to prevent it from moving around.

This concept (bike not pictured) attaches to the car door handles and allows you to mount the bike on the side of the car. There are many potential issues with this design, since it might prevent you from opening doors, and may damage the bike if you are driving to close on that side. It also may not be stable.

Below is an example of a spill proof coffee cup. Please note, the straw will leak when the cup is rotated 90 deg from the angle shown. The cup will leak if squeezed and the hot liquid emerging from the straw will burn one's mouth.

Please study the problem and this example. You will be asked to come up with your own designs later.
